data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's cross-city modulator (evaporative contrast via vegetation/aridity) is internally inconsistent with observed arid-city UHI: it asserts drier surroundings reduce the urban-rural evaporative contrast and thus weaken the nocturnal gap, but arid cities like Phoenix exhibit large nocturnal UHI. If the single best mechanism must explain the larger gap in some cities, an evaporative-deficit mechanism that predicts weaker UHI for the very cities that show strong UHI fails the problem.
